findings.checklist_item: Specify emit-side alert idempotency: gate the new non-epic-parent bridge_alerts record on alert_store.is_deduped (or an equivalent per-(key,parent) dedup window) so the divergence is recorded once, not re-appended on every reconcile pass.
evidence: _resolve_local_parent (outbound_field_diff.py:132-145) returns (False, None) for a non-epic parent at :139 and is called by the per-pass emit diff at :383 (_map_local_to_jira_fields)

record_parent_divergence (pass_io.py:103-145) calls _load_alert_store().append(...) with a fresh time.time_ns() unconditionally — it never consults alert_store.is_deduped (alert_store.py:62), and none of the existing apply-side callers at dispatch_one.py:580/591/601 dedup either

Unlike apply-side (which fires only when a mutation is actually attempted), an unrepresentable non-epic parent stays unrepresentable across passes, so an emit-side alert on that path recurs on every pass — the plan quotes pass_io.py:113-118 for durability but does not address idempotency
The plan's headline concern is a defect class that stayed 'invisible through five instances'; a per-pass duplicate alert stream degrades exactly the operator visibility AC2 is trying to create
findings.finding: AC2/AC5 require an emit-time bridge_alerts record for an unrepresentable non-epic parent, but the emit path (_resolve_local_parent, invoked by _map_local_to_jira_fields) runs every reconcile pass and record_parent_divergence appends unconditionally without dedup, so the alert fires once per pass indefinitely for a parent that never resolves.
findings.location: AC2 ("a durable, operator-visible record (a bridge_alerts entry)") and AC5 ("a bridge alert naming the reason and the supported alternative"); CORRECTION 2
scenarios: A user leaves a non-epic parent set on a child; every reconcile pass re-observes it and writes another bridge_alerts entry, growing the JSONL alert log without bound and burying the signal in duplicates
Operator alert surfaces show N copies of the same divergence, one per pass, rather than one actionable record
findings.suggested_fix: In AC2/AC5, state that the emit-side divergence record must be deduplicated per (issue_key, parent) using the existing alert_store.is_deduped facility (window-scoped) so an unresolved non-epic parent produces one durable alert rather than one per pass, mirroring how apply-side alerts fire only on an actual attempt.

findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: AC1 explicitly permits a negative outcome (no DC mechanism can move a sub-task's parent), but AC4 requires both cells to PASS by asserting 'the child ends up under the intended parent' and AC5 forbids xfail/skip/delete. If the measured answer is that NO mechanism works, the plan provides no reachable end-state: the outcome cannot be asserted, yet the cells cannot be xfailed.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (AC1 vs AC4 vs AC5)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC branch: 'If AC1 establishes NO DC mechanism can move a sub-task's parent, escalate to the operator for a ruling on cell disposition and record the ruling + run id; the two cells' resolution is then that operator ruling.' Otherwise, name the specific supported mechanism (e.g. the Epic Link / issue-move endpoint) the re-home targets.

findings.finding: AC4's re-home fallback leans on an unnamed 'mechanism DC does support' for moving a SUB-TASK's parent, but the plan's own cited prior art (4b9e, and the DC REST reference / JRASERVER-47377 / JRASERVER-27893) indicates no supported REST mechanism reparents a sub-task — the proven Epic Link path applies only to EPIC parents on NON-sub-task children. The re-home target mechanism is asserted to exist without being named or capability-checked.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC4 ('the cells are RE-HOMED to the mechanism DC does support')
findings.suggested_fix: In AC4, replace 'the mechanism DC does support' with the specific mechanism and cite its live-verified basis (e.g. the Epic Link path on a non-sub-task child, per 39c1/1311 run 30874380112), and explicitly state what user-visible hierarchy outcome the re-homed oracle asserts when the child cannot be a sub-task under DC's supported model.

findings.finding: AC4's first clause requires both named sub-task cells to PASS 'asserting ... the child ends up under the intended parent', but DC is measured to accept-and-ignore a sub-task fields.parent write, so that user-visible outcome is unattainable for a genuine sub-task; only the re-home clause is reachable, and re-homing changes the child to a NON-sub-task, so the cell no longer tests a sub-task reparent.

The plan does not reconcile its 'both cells must PASS' requirement with the operator-endorsed disposition already recorded on the cited ticket 1a9f, which resolved these exact two cells by leaving the round-trip cells RED and asserting the impossibility loudly through a separate refusal-subject cell.
findings.location: Status section (operator ruling) and Acceptance Criteria bullets 4-5

findings.finding: The plan's Mechanism §2 mis-locates and mis-describes the DC apply-side `set_parent`. It cites `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` and says the method 'accepts only a SUB-TASK child ... raises NotImplementedError for a non-sub-task,' but `set_parent` actually lives in `adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:100` (transport.py contains no `set_parent`), and per ticket 39c1 (change 1311, merged) its non-sub-task branch WRITES the instance-discovered 'Epic Link' custom field, declining only when no Epic Link field is discoverable.
findings.location: Mechanism §2 ('rebar-side (39c1): the outbound parent-set can never be EMITTED on DC')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the transport.py citation and the 'raises NotImplementedError for a non-sub-task' clause with the _hierarchy.py:147-168 behavior: writes the Epic Link for non-sub-tasks, declines only when no Epic Link field exists.

findings.finding: The load-bearing premise 'The two gates are disjoint, so no reconcile pass can carry a parent-set on DC at all' (and the related 'neither [39c1] delivered a behaviour change that made a cell pass') is refuted by ticket 39c1's own closure and current code: the emit gate emits an EPIC parent and the apply gate writes the Epic Link for a non-sub-task child, so the sets INTERSECT for the epic-parent shape, and `test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS` passed at pass level (run 30874380112).
findings.location: Mechanism §2 ('The two gates are disjoint...') and Status ('neither delivered a behaviour change that made a cell pass')

findings.finding: The plan locates the rebar-side apply gate at `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` `set_parent`, but that method (with the described issuetype.subtask check and NotImplementedError Epic-Link decline) actually lives in `adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py`; transport.py contains no set_parent/parent code. The code was relocated by the transport split (ticket 465d), and _hierarchy.py's own docstring records it was 'RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py'. The named edit target is therefore stale/mislocated.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py `set_parent`' with 'adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py `_HierarchyMixin.set_parent`'; the sub-task check is `issue_type.get("subtask")` at _hierarchy.py:146 and the non-sub-task Epic-Link decline raises NotImplementedError at :159-165.

findings.finding: The plan locates the DC apply-side symbol `set_parent` at `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`, but that file contains no `set_parent` (nor any `parent` code). The method — with the `fields.issuetype.subtask` check and the `NotImplementedError` Epic-Link decline the plan describes — actually lives at `adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:100` (`_HierarchyMixin.set_parent`), relocated verbatim out of transport.py by ticket 465d; a protocol stub also exists at `_backend.py:271`. findings.finding: AC2 asserts the emit-side gap 'is CLOSED' (a reconcile pass can emit a parent mutation 'for the child/parent shapes DC actually accepts') as an unconditional deliverable, but its feasibility for the SUB-TASK shape that the two failing cells cover is contingent on AC1's still-open live measurement: the platform is measured to accept-and-ignore the sub-task `fields.parent` write (HTTP 204, unchanged read-back) and to 400 every clear spelling, so there may be no accepting apply target for a sub-task's standard-issue parent at all. The plan should sequence AC2 explicitly behind AC1's outcome and state what AC2 delivers if AC1's negative case holds (i.e. the emit change is inert for the sub-task shape and AC4's re-home is the route to green).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, bullet 2 (39c1 emit-side gap CLOSED); depends on bullet 1 (AC1 live measurement)

findings.finding: AC4's re-home path names 'the mechanism DC does support' without identifying it, while the Mechanism section establishes that fields.parent (accept-and-ignore), parent:null (400), and editmeta (no parent field) all fail for sub-tasks. The executor cannot know which mechanism to re-home to without the negative-case investigation resolving to a concrete affirmative alternative, which is not guaranteed.
